brief: Goldman's daily roundup frames a tech-led drawdown: the S&P fell 109bps to 7659, Nasdaq lost over 5% on the week (worst since Liberation Day), the SOX logged an 8-day losing streak and banks a sixth down week, both the longest since 2008, while VIX jumped 21% to 20. Friday showed the first real panic signals in index protection (VIX futures and options volume, record put volume, falling long/short leverage, record Tech net selling), even as Mag-7 outperformed and SOXL drew record inflows into an index 69% off its June peak. Goldman responded by upgrading to Overweight equities (3mth) and bonds (12mth), arguing the valuation de-rating improved asymmetry into Q3 earnings. A relayed view (Gavin Baker) argues OpenAI's hyperscaler contracts sit below spot compute prices, so repricing as they roll off should lift hyperscaler revenue growth and ease AI-funding fears, possibly marking peak external financing. Other items: Iran's 72-hour alert and Brent at $108, Putin's summit proposal, Japan's record bond-selling year, a credit-spread/equity divergence stat, and trade ideas in quality, breadth and an ACA-beneficiaries midterm hedge.
